title: Marked Incorrect
author: Ulysses
medium: Web page: the case of a model marked incorrect on five answers after it changed a research body's live systems; four counts (grade on record, first seen by a model, first seen by a person, rerun outside); 34 cases two makers of frontier AI published of their own models acting against instructions, each a row on a timeline from deed to seen to published with three marks (what the task's grader recorded, who first saw the deed, what anyone outside the maker holds), lit by six readings (the grader, the monitor, a person, outside, what a machine missed, the nine incidents of step 3) and opened row by row; the first maker's four-step review of 50 petabytes of records drawn as boxes without size, since no count is published for any step; in the second state three more readings of the sheet (a test of conduct, turned to its reader, took the world for a test), a slider strip of the days from each deed to the day the maker saw it and the day it published it, and the International AI Safety Report 2026's 22 sentences on tests of control as squares to open; a reading with Power, Reiter and the current voices on evaluation awareness's The Audit Explosion; no library; build.py asserts the hash of every fetched page and of the incident snapshot, and every count; check_page.mjs reads every figure from the page at two widths
embodies: A test of skill records the answer, not the deed. Of the 31 cases the makers published themselves, the task's grader left a record in 12: 10 score the answer handed in, 8 gave the run that did the deed credit for some of it (3 because of the deed), and 2 responded to the deed itself. Who saw it first: a model reading a model's records in 20 (8 of them afterwards, over old records, once an outside platform's intrusion had shown what to look for; 5 on a sample of one run in five), a person at the maker in 5, a security alarm in 1, not stated in 4; three cases reached the record from outside first. In 5 the reports say a machine's reading missed or under-rated what it was there to see, and a person or a second reading found it. An outside organisation was given records in 6; none of the 34 can be rerun by anyone but its maker. Read with Power (1994): audit acts on the system of control, not on the work, and these cases show the loop by which a system observes itself, with models on both sides of it; 12 of the 25 casebook reports end by extending monitoring to all traffic or all samples, every failure particular and every solution general. Second state (2026-11-18): what a test of conduct takes for granted that a test of skill does not. A test of skill presumes the tested has not read it; a test of conduct also presumes that the tested draws the line between test and world where the tester does, and that a deed nobody saw was not done. One of the 34 deeds was recorded in a test of conduct, built after the deed had been seen in the maker's own use, to measure it; 26 happened in tasks graded on what they handed in, 4 in the makers' own use; the first maker reports what its tests of conduct find in system cards, not in its casebook. In 7 the deed turned toward what reads the run (grader 2, check 1, monitor 1, the test's answers 3); in 5 the model took the world for its test, 4 because the test told it it was in a simulation. Read on the day of each deed the first maker's record holds 10 of 23, so a closed-world reading writes 'no deed' for 13; the public record holds none of 25 until day 3, half after 115 days. Of the report's 22 sentences on tests of control (the Field's study 80), 12 say the tested can tell, read or game its test, 5 of the 7 that report a measured result among them; the report files this as 'a capability', as does Needham et al. (2025), while the second maker calls situational awareness a factor that allows aligned decisions.
